title: Simplifying and Accelerating NOR Flash I/O Stack for RAM-Restricted Microcontrollers
problem: NOR flash file systems for RAM-restricted microcontrollers migrate block-level data organization and wear leveling logic from RAM into flash, introducing fine-grained block-level management that causes frequent index updates and full-device scans. This results in severe I/O amplification that worsens when the management layers are decoupled across the I/O stack.
motivation: IoT microcontrollers have extreme RAM budgets (tens of KB) but must use NOR flash for persistent storage; the current approach of emulating a block-layer abstraction in flash creates unsustainable write amplification and latency that degrades device lifetime and responsiveness.
method: The paper redesigns the NOR flash I/O stack to eliminate the decoupled block-level management abstraction, instead employing coarse-grained, integrated data organization that reduces index update frequency. Wear leveling is restructured to operate at a coarser granularity aligned with the NOR flash erase unit, avoiding the fine-grained scanning overhead. The resulting simplified stack collapses previously separate software layers to reduce coupling and I/O amplification jointly.
key_novelty: Collapsing decoupled block-level management layers into a unified, coarse-grained I/O stack design that jointly eliminates index-update amplification and wear-leveling scan overhead for NOR flash on microcontrollers.
contributions: Analysis of I/O amplification sources in existing NOR flash file systems for RAM-restricted microcontrollers.
Redesigned I/O stack that integrates data organization and wear leveling at coarse granularity.
Reduction of NOR flash index update frequency and device scanning overhead.
Evaluation demonstrating improved I/O performance and reduced write amplification on microcontroller workloads.

metrics.other: I/O amplification reduction (details in full paper)

baselines: existing NOR flash file systems (e.g., SPIFFS, LittleFS)
limitations: Specific I/O amplification reduction numbers and comparison breadth are not stated in the abstract.
